{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-or-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ef821a93d9c2bad5a2968a321db1aaee23cb9fcb90eed2102da3844547b7c4c2","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-or-class-c:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"ce8335c1d96ff7ed209bf236ba9a56fe92dfebd915bc0e2fa7fb830ee03f0f09","source_liveness_sha256":"c4da479589e7933e4eef7366086dfcc48a420303d0089cb0ea19ad9137abec1d"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Testing: vision, Class C knowledge test and drive test","heading":"C2 — Testing confusables: office versus online knowledge test, retest waits, drive test waivers and vehicle readiness","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Testing confusables: office versus online knowledge test, retest waits, drive test waivers and vehicle readiness
Confusable pairs from the testing chapter, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A03
Retest timing depends on why you failed: an ordinary office failure may allow a same-day retest if the office has capacity, but a cheating failure bars any retest for 90 days. [A03]
Why it matters: group knowledge test; confusable ordinary failure versus cheating failure; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A04
Online retests are capped differently from office retests: online you get two tries per 24 hours and four in all before you must go to an office. [A04]
Why it matters: group knowledge test; confusable office retest versus online retest; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A05
A failed drive test cannot be retaken the same day; the earliest retake is the next business day. [A05]
Why it matters: group drive test; confusable knowledge-test retest versus drive-test retest; difficulty easy.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A03
At an office, authorized translators may enter the knowledge-test area, whereas a translator is never allowed inside the car during the drive test. [A03]
Why it matters: group conduct rules; confusable knowledge test area versus drive test vehicle; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A03
A paper foreign-language translation dictionary may be used during an office knowledge test only with permission, while a DMV manual, notes and electronic devices are never allowed. [A03]
Why it matters: group conduct rules; confusable permitted aid versus banned aid; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A04
The online knowledge test must be taken on a desktop or laptop with keyboard, mouse and webcam, unlike the office test, which is given on a DMV touch-screen monitor. [A04]
Why it matters: group knowledge test; confusable online device versus office device; difficulty easy.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A04
The proctor rule applies only to online test takers under 18, and the proctor must be over 21, not merely a licensed adult of any age. [A04]
Why it matters: group knowledge test; confusable applicant age versus proctor age; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A02
Wearing glasses or contacts for the vision test does not fail you; it adds a corrective-lens requirement to your driving privilege. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable lens restriction versus failing the vision test; difficulty easy.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A02
Unlike the other tests, the vision test carries no fee, and failing it leads to a referral form for a licensed vision specialist rather than an automatic denial. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable free vision test versus fee-based tests; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A04
A drive test waiver for a new resident needs an out-of-state license that is still valid or expired less than one year, and that license is surrendered. [A04]
Why it matters: group waivers; confusable new-resident waiver versus driver-education waiver; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A04
A drive test waiver based on driver education needs proof of an ODOT-Approved course completed within the past two years. [A04]
Why it matters: group waivers; confusable two-year course window versus one-year license expiry window; difficulty hard.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A05
Missing proof of insurance and a failed vehicle equipment check both force a rescheduled drive test, even though neither involves your driving. [A05]
Why it matters: group vehicle readiness; confusable paperwork failure versus equipment failure; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A06
Traction tires or chains, wipers, headlights, taillights and a defroster are required on the test vehicle only when the weather calls for them, unlike the always-required items such as brake lights and a horn. [A06]
Why it matters: group vehicle readiness; confusable always-required versus weather-dependent equipment; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A06
Booking through a certified Third Party Tester can be faster or offer extra days and times, but it may cost more than testing at DMV. [A06]
Why it matters: group appointments; confusable DMV appointment versus Third Party Tester; difficulty easy.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A06
The six-month permit-holding rule applies to applicants under 18 who are seeking a driver license, not to adult applicants. [A06]
Why it matters: group eligibility; confusable minor applicant versus adult applicant; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A01
The manual addresses only the Class C non-commercial driving privilege, so commercial license requirements are outside its scope. [A01]
Why it matters: group scope; confusable Class C versus commercial classes; difficulty easy.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0008]
